references.text: Ezekiel mentions the sword as one of God's instruments of punishment, as seen here in Leviticus where the sword avenges covenant breaking.
Jeremiah describes pestilence (דֶּבֶר) as one of God's means of punishment, along with the sword and famine.
Ezekiel prophesies about pestilence and bloodshed as punishment, reflecting the threats in Leviticus.
Deuteronomy repeats the threats of pestilence as punishment for covenant breaking, parallel to Leviticus 26.
Moses' song mentions the sword from outside as punishment, corresponding with the enemy's sword in Leviticus.
Jeremiah prophesies about being handed over into the enemy's hand, using the same expression found in Leviticus 26:25.
Ezekiel mentions the three punishments: the sword outside, pestilence and famine within the cities.
The threat of pestilence and loss in war as a consequence of disobedience, parallel to Leviticus 26.
Pestilence as God's instrument of punishment against Israel, fulfilling the threats from Leviticus.
The choice between pestilence, sword or famine as punishment, reflecting the covenant curses.
